properties.title: Transition-Based Digital Twin Modelling for Alzheimer's Disease under Sparse Longitudinal Data

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Two-branch digital twin framework for Alzheimer's disease forecasting from ADNI with what-if covariate perturbation.
A transition MLP for next-visit prediction and a BiLSTM-Attention branch with MC dropout intervals and covariate what-if analysis.

properties.algorithm: MLP over adjacent-visit pairs with mRMR features

properties.population: ADNI participants with cognitive, clinical and MRI features

properties.description: ADNI, 760 subjects and 2801 records at six-month intervals to 60 months
Held-out subject-level test of both branches, 76 subjects

properties.algorithm: BiLSTM-Attention sequence branch with MC dropout intervals
Multinomial logistic regression on the mRMR feature space

Accordingly, the system is retained as a supporting component even though held-out next-visit and 24-month forecasts are evaluated (Table 1) and observational covariate perturbations are illustrated (Fig. 5).

legacy_cells.B: Transition-Based Digital Twin Modelling for Alzheimer's Disease under Sparse Longitudinal Data
legacy_cells.C: Huang, Yinyu, Zhang, Yilin, Michopoulou, Sofia, Kipps, Christopher, Attar, Rahman
legacy_cells.S: Whether adjacent-visit and longitudinal multimodal patient data can forecast future MMSE and diagnostic category, including subject-level trajectories.
legacy_cells.T: ADNI longitudinal cohort; 760 participants after exclusions; targets include cognitively normal, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer’s disease categories.
legacy_cells.AI: Clinical variables; cognitive assessments/scores (including MMSE and diagnosis); FreeSurfer-derived MRI structural phenotypes
legacy_cells.BL: Six-month visit intervals; adjacent-visit transition predicts the next six-month visit; follow-up aligned from baseline to 60 months.
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted MMSE scores; diagnosis categories/probabilities; sequence-branch predictive intervals and what-if trajectories.
legacy_cells.BT: MMSE regression head and diagnosis (DX) classification head.
legacy_cells.BV: BiLSTM-Attention branch: SmoothL1 loss for MMSE regression and focal loss for DX classification.
legacy_cells.CR: Held-out test-set DX calibration: multiclass Brier score 0.1423, Top-1 ECE 0.0185, and macro class-wise ECE 0.0177.
legacy_cells.FN: The local-transition MLP achieved MMSE RMSE 2.149 and MAE 1.529; diagnosis accuracy 0.906, AUC 0.976 and macro-F1 0.908. BiLSTM-attention values were RMSE 2.687, MAE 1.926, accuracy 0.806, AUC 0.928 and F1 0.798; sample construction and horizons differ, limiting direct architectural conclusions.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF title and abstract, pp. 1–2; Introduction, pp. 2–3; Methods §§2.1–2.3, pp. 3–5; Results §§3.1–3.5 and Tables 1–3, pp. 5–10; Discussion, p. 11; Conclusion, p. 12; References, pp. 12–13. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I were left unchanged; no direct PDF contradiction requiring correction was found. M is not applicable because the paper is included. The paper demonstrates predictive adjacent-visit transitions and sequence forecasts, but feature perturbations are not identified treatment actions or causal counterfactuals; AA records the authors’ stated what-if capability separately. Figure 5 extraction has scrambled layout/text, so no figure-derived quantitative details were entered; table values used are readable. Evidence QA: 20/24 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (83.3%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 23 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 1 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All 13 PDF pages were read as extracted text (including Conclusion and References on pp. 12-13) and rendered page images were visually inspected for pages 4, 6, 7, 8, and 10 (Figs. 1-5, Tables 1-3).
The legacy row was read from the root workbook (read only). Saved API drafts for B098 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass, no independent human review.
notes: Two-branch AD digital twin on ADNI (760 subjects, 76 held-out). The MLP next-visit transition model reaches MMSE RMSE 2.149 and diagnosis ACC 0.906, and the BiLSTM-Attention 24-month branch reaches RMSE 2.687 and ACC 0.806, with MC dropout intervals and covariate what-if cases. The branches differ in horizon and sample construction, so the claim that transition modelling is more data-efficient is confounded. What-if analysis is observational. Classified L1, supporting component, R2. Source points: single cohort, interpolation to a regular grid, no interval coverage.
